title: Thannitus
desc: A 19-year-old student obsessed with death begins to hear a sound that follows him everywhere he goes. He obsesses over it, assuming it’s the sound of his death—but as he does, he unknowingly walks into the very thing he tried to prevent.
notes: Produced and screened at Northwestern’s National High School Institute to an audience of about 170.
Built around a sound-centric approach to the script.
Submitted to YoungArts.
alt: Behind the scenes on the set of Thannitus: an actor at a desk wearing headphones, a camera monitor and boom microphone in the foreground, lit in blue.
photo: On set during the filming of Thannitus.

title: Spar
desc: Two teenage martial artists are sparring when one accidentally paralyzes the other. In the aftermath, two former friends must come to terms with what they carry.
notes: Produced and screened at Northwestern’s National High School Institute to an audience of about 170.
An official director’s cut is planned for film-festival submission.
alt: Two shirtless boxers sparring on a dark stage under blue and magenta light, during the filming of Spar.
photo: On set during the filming of Spar.
warning: Contains strong language and a serious injury.
subtitle: Block C

title: Continuum
desc: A man haunted by the memory of his dead lover attempts to dream his pain away. Set in a dystopia where one company sells a lifetime of dreams in one night—but when the man asks for the dream he cannot control, he finds himself in the middle of what he’s been trying to escape.
alt: A pale watch dial with fine tick marks and two hands on a dark blue field, a single bright blue point at its center.

title: Sunny Side Up
desc: It’s the night shift at a diner: a 19-year-old waiter who’s aged out of foster care and a homeless eight-year-old in the corner booth find a brief moment of connection.
notes: Not yet produced or submitted.
alt: A diner window glowing amber at night, with a pink neon sign reading Open 24 Hours.

title: Truly I Tell You
desc: Nico, a 12-year-old with a troubled home life, becomes fixated on the idea of baptism: that by being submerged, one can wash away their sins. One afternoon, he sneaks into a pool and baptizes himself: he closes his eyes, whispers a prayer, and sinks below the surface. But he doesn’t come back up.
notes: Opens with an epigraph from T.S. Eliot’s The Waste Land.
Not yet produced or submitted.
alt: An empty swimming pool seen from above, turquoise tile and shifting light.
warning: Contains strong language and distressing content.

title: White Elephants
desc: Josh and Jade have dinner in their apartment while she gets ready for a party. The rain gets heavier. Neither one says what the evening is really about.
notes: Not yet produced or submitted.
alt: Rain streaking down a window at night, blurred warm lights behind it.

title: The Switchman
desc: An adaptation of the short story, in development. A lone railroad operator whose whole job is a switch, the trains that keep passing, and the question of whether responsibility needs free will.
notes: Loosely based on Kafka’s The Trial.
Adapted from the short story of the same name.
alt: Railroad tracks converging toward a single lit window in a dim, reddish room.

title: Forever Young
desc: After a car accident leaves him with anterograde amnesia, 19-year-old Simon is forever stuck thinking every day is his 19th birthday. As his fiancee, best friend, and family move on without him, the film asks what is owed to someone who cannot move forward with them.
notes: My first feature, estimated at forty to fifty minutes, now in writing and pre-production.
alt: Concentric ghost arcs of light turning around a single warm point at the center.

title: Landfall
desc: Soldiers drop from airships onto a frozen shore in a war led by a messiah whom no one is allowed to question. The story follows one soldier among thousands.
notes: Not previously published or submitted.
alt: Airships hanging in gray mist above a frozen shore.

title: A Home Beyond
desc: The Earth is dying. A mother, Lucia, tries to carry her son Oliver away from it, toward a place that might still be a home.
notes: The prologue and original inspiration for the novella The Lighthouse.
Submitted to Stone Soup.
alt: A rocket trail rising white-hot from a burning city skyline against a dark, starry sky.

title: The Steps Beyond Time
desc: An allegory about a ruthless rich man and a kind receptionist who both die and descend a staircase where every step relives a memory of what someone said about them.
notes: Gold Key, Scholastic Art & Writing Awards.
Submitted to Stone Soup.
alt: A white staircase rising toward a bright, blurred light.

title: The Switchman
desc: Inspired by the writing and philosophy of Camus and the logic of Kafka, a Switchman takes instructions from the bureaucratic Control as he directs trains down a track. A story dealing with themes of free will, responsibility for our choices, and the meaning(lessness) of life.
notes: Inspired by existentialist and absurdist work in the vein of Camus and Kafka.
Submitted to YoungArts, The Adroit Journal, and Stone Soup.
alt: Railroad tracks converging toward a single lit window in a dim, reddish room.

title: A Knight of Silver
desc: A darkly comedic anti-chivalry story: a knight is forced to deal with the gruesome and unsightly clean-up after he kills another knight in single combat. A series of (mis)adventures ensues.
notes: Submitted to the Blue Marble Review and Stone Soup.
alt: A sword planted point-down in dark grass under a pale, glowing moon.

title: A Knight of Silver
desc: A longer version of the flash fiction, currently being written.
alt: A sword planted point-down in dark grass under a pale, glowing moon.
subtitle: Long version

title: Pain and Power
desc: It begins with the rare men who rise above the fray and change the course of history, then turns to one ordinary man who lived under the regime of the Dominion and witnessed power at its ugliest and most beautiful.
alt: A bare road converging at a flat horizon under a pale, dusty sky, one tiny figure in the distance.

title: The Last of the Mastermen
desc: An old man, one hand still on the pommel of his sword, makes his way along a worn path and stops to rest. The Mastermen of the title are long dead.
alt: Two small figures standing on a dusty plain under a hazy, golden sky.

title: The Lighthouse
desc: A multi-perspective science-fiction novella about a crew of genetically-modified children sent to found a perfect civilization on a new planet, following how the utopia repeats the violence it was sent to escape.
notes: Builds on ideas from The Iliad and Paradise Lost.
Estimated at about 150 pages; I hope to finish and self-publish it by December 2026.
alt: A lighthouse at the end of a long pier at dusk, a pink band of cloud above still water.

title: Powerborn
desc: The first novel of the Powerborn Trilogy, estimated at about 300 pages and currently on an extended hiatus.
alt: Three jagged bolts of lightning, blue, white and violet, against a dark sky.

title: The Question of Us
desc: A long essay on the questions we cannot stop asking: what came before us, what consciousness is, and what it means to live inside an unexplained universe. It ends on a single word, wonder.
notes: Not yet published or submitted.
alt: A spiral galaxy glowing at the center of a dark starfield.

title: The Sublime and the Scientific
desc: Through close readings of Galileo’s Sidereus Nuncius, Neil deGrasse Tyson’s Astrophysics for People in a Hurry, NASA’s Hubble imagery, Stapledon’s Star Maker, Clarke’s 2001, and Nolan’s Interstellar, I argue that astronomy presents the astronomical sublime as something resolveable by reason, while science-fiction literature intentionally stays within the moment of irresolution.
notes: Written under the mentorship of Oxford Research Fellow Dr. Diana Little.
Submitted to the Oxford Journal of Student Scholarship.
alt: Dark columns of gas in a teal and amber nebula, scattered with stars.
subtitle: How Science Fiction Captures, Transforms, and Reinvents Awe

title: Tireless Sun
desc: A walk down the hill toward the beach, an ordinary sunset that feels new, and the wondering about humanity’s place in the universe that follows it home.
notes: Submitted to YoungArts, The Adroit Journal, Stone Soup, and the Blue Marble Review.
alt: A pale gold sun setting over dark hills with a single small house on the right.

title: Dreaming With Eyes Wide Open
desc: Traces my life as a reader and writer back to sounding out my first word at age three.
notes: Honorable Mention, Scholastic Art & Writing Awards.
Submitted to The Adroit Journal.
alt: A single wide-open eye whose pupil is filled with stars.

title: Human; Assisted
desc: Argues that AI is a tool that extends human creativity rather than replacing it.
notes: Honorable Mention, Scholastic Art & Writing Awards.
alt: A warm hand-drawn line weaving through a cold network of connected points.
